other_failure_modes.name: Data leakage in cross-validation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes dataset-wide statistics (such as imputation medians and frequency encodings) on the entire training set before performing the cross-validation split. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the validation score artificially optimistic.

other_failure_modes.name: Inconsistent feature engineering based on dataset statistics
other_failure_modes.description: The agent conditionally applies transformations (like log1p) independently on the train and test sets based on their respective skewness. If a column's skewness differs slightly between splits, this can lead to a mismatched feature space (e.g., a feature being generated in train but not in test), causing errors during inference.

other_failure_modes.name: Test data leakage in categorical encoding
other_failure_modes.description: The agent fits a LabelEncoder on the union of the training and test sets. While common in competitive data science, this is a bad practice for production models as it assumes all future test categories are known at training time.

summary: The agent provides a robust and well-structured machine learning pipeline, featuring extensive domain-specific feature engineering, target log-transformation, and an optimized model ensemble. However, it ignores the temporal nature of the dataset by using a random KFold split instead of a time-based validation scheme, introducing look-ahead bias. Additionally, it computes imputation and frequency encoding statistics prior to cross-validation, leading to data leakage between folds, and uses a risky conditional feature engineering approach that could result in mismatched train and test schemas.
